title: The four cosets of ⟨4⟩ in ℤ₁₂
caption: Adding 1, 2 or 3 to ⟨4⟩ = {0, 4, 8} turns the triangle round the clock. The four triangles use every number exactly once, so there are 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cosets, and 1 + ⟨4⟩ has order 4 in the quotient: ℤ₁₂/⟨4⟩ ≅ ℤ₄.
alt: A clock face with 12 points. Four equilateral triangles, {0, 4, 8}, {1, 5, 9}, {2, 6, 10} and {3, 7, 11}, in four colours, each point in exactly one triangle.
description: The subgroup ⟨4⟩ = {0, 4, 8} is a triangle on the clock.
Adding 1 turns it to {1, 5, 9}, adding 2 to {2, 6, 10} and adding 3 to {3, 7, 11}.
The four triangles are the cosets: congruent, with no point shared, and together they use all 12 numbers.
Adding 1 four times (0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4) returns to ⟨4⟩, so the quotient has order 4: ℤ₁₂/⟨4⟩ ≅ ℤ₄.
